Swiss Army Bench 0.0.1: the first beta test. The version starts again at 0.0.1 with the new name; the
SwissArmyGrid releases (1.0.0 to 1.6.0) came before it. Everything below passed its tests, and now needs real
use: report what breaks or feels wrong.

**SwissArmyGrid is now Swiss Army Bench.** The package, wheel and uv tool are `swissarmybench`, the import
is `import swissarmybench as sab`, and the commands are `swissarmybench`, `sab`, `swissarmybench-mcp` and
`swissarmybench-context`. The old names (`import swissarmygrid`, `swissarmygrid`, `sag`, the `%sag_run`,
`%%sag_table` and `%%sag_html` magics, `SWISSARMYGRID_*` variables, old notebooks, blades and tangs) keep
working for this release and go in the next one. On its first start the server moves `~/.swissarmygrid`
to `~/.swissarmybench`; saved passwords are found under the old name. The installers remove the old
`swissarmygrid` uv tool first. Update the VS Code extension too. The README's "Renamed from
SwissArmyGrid" has the details.

## Install the beta

On Windows, in PowerShell (installs uv if needed, then the server as a uv tool):

```powershell
irm https://github.com/DylanCodyBrown/SwissArmyBench/releases/download/v0.0.1/install.ps1 | iex
```

On macOS or Linux:

```bash
curl -LsSf https://github.com/DylanCodyBrown/SwissArmyBench/releases/download/v0.0.1/install.sh | sh
```

Or by hand, from the wheel:

```bash
uv tool install --force "swissarmybench-0.0.1-py3-none-any.whl[server]"   # the server, from the wheel
uv pip install swissarmybench-0.0.1-py3-none-any.whl                      # the client, in a project
```

Or the installer beside the wheel: `sh install.sh ./swissarmybench-0.0.1-py3-none-any.whl` (macOS,
Linux) or `install.ps1 .\swissarmybench-0.0.1-py3-none-any.whl` (Windows).

## New in this beta (the last days' work)

- **Beta mode:** right-click anything and "Leave a note…"; a redacted beta log (no data, no SQL, no secrets).
  "Export beta log…" in Settings writes one zip to send back. One switch turns both off.
- **Export as one Python script or one notebook:** any notebook as a self-contained automation, with its
  connections, the vault lookup (managed identity, standard library only), the grid steps as DuckDB SQL and any
  Add API client inlined. It runs with plain `python` or any Jupyter scheduler (papermill, nbconvert).
- **Add API:** an OpenAPI document or a short form becomes `API_<name>.py` and a connection in one step. API keys,
  OAuth 2.0, JWT, AWS Signature Version 4, Google and Firebase tokens; presets for Azure Function Apps, AWS
  Lambda and Google.
- **The Workbench:** tab groups and a Data panel; kind colours (app violet, notebook blue, script green); four
  modes (App: Properties, wiring, Starters gallery, State, preview; Notebook: Outline, run order, Present;
  Script: run settings, Run as scheduled, history; Data: the dictionary and lineage).
- **The Streamlit canvas:** a Streamlit app built from notebook cells (Python, Markdown with live `{{ values }}`
  and Mermaid, HTML), pages, Play in place, controllers with defaults, Test this page, Save as zip with data.py.
- **Lineage:** right-click a block or cell for the flow back to the data, with live values; approved outputs that
  turn a notebook into its own test (`--check-approved` headless).
- **Starters:** 111 ready-made blades and snippets: Power BI actions, Excel, files, DAX, HTML, Markdown, Streamlit,
  Components (your own HTML and JavaScript in Streamlit), Controllers, Text and layout.
- **Connections:** a Power BI workspace with DAX cells; your own Python as a connection; key vaults by your sign-in
  or managed identity.
- **For agents:** 255 tools; a short index read first (`swissarmybench://index`).

## New

- **The Workbench**, in a window of its own (the grid page's Workbench tab): notebooks (`.ipynb`) and
  Python scripts in an IPython kernel on your computer, laid out like RStudio:
  - the source, its console under it, Variables on the right; splitters; a status bar; the side bar
    (Ctrl+B) with connections, blades and the data explorer; a picture or chart goes to the Sandbox
    with one click;
  - F5 runs a script as Python would; Ctrl+Enter runs the whole statement at the cursor and moves on;
    every document has a console that takes several lines; `input()` asks in place;
  - Jupyter's command mode in notebooks (A, B, D D, Z, Y, M, S), run above and below, undo;
  - a command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) over every action; completion from the kernel and, in SQL cells,
    from the data explorer's catalog; F1 help;
  - **the error panel**: what went wrong in plain words, where in your code, the failing expression's
    values at that moment, one-click fixes (the close name, the missing import, install the package,
    run the cell that makes a name), the failing expression underlined in the editor with its message
    at the line's end and Ctrl+. fixes;
  - **Send to the agent**: right-click an error or selected code; it reaches your agent with your next
    message (the plugin's prompt hook) or through its `agent_inbox` tool;
  - a notebook's own virtual environment, made in a dialog and remembered;
  - open documents come back after a reload.
- **Connections**, apart from blades: databases and files, added with a form per type (the code
  underneath), tested before saving; passwords from the keyring, an environment variable or a key
  vault. Every connection is in every Workbench notebook and script by its name.
- **The SQL cell**: `%%sql <connection>` runs a cell on a connection (its own SQL for a database,
  DuckDB over a file's tables), in the Workbench, Jupyter and IPython.
- **The Sandbox**: a dashboard of resizable cards (Plotly, ECharts, Vega-Lite, Graphviz, Mermaid,
  pictures, tables, notes), pages and Print to PDF, saved dashboards, twenty themes, `sab.sandbox()`.
- **The Analyze menu**: fit test (Benford), outliers, odds, find predictors, linear and logistic
  regression with what-if, time series and forecast; "Show the math" for every result; your own
  analyses as blades.
- **Compare**: a diff mode and the tie-out report. **Relationships**: tangs and the relationship
  finder. **Packs**: blades and tangs shared as a Claude Code plugin marketplace.
- **The VS Code extension is slim**: Swiss Army Bench's tools in VS Code's agent mode, and an Open
  Swiss Army Bench button. Install Swiss Army Bench with uv first; the extension no longer starts, carries or
  updates the server, or pushes files.
- **The agent can do whatever you can** through the MCP (177 tools), the Workbench included; it never
  sees a password's value, and its exports still wait for your Allow.

## Known

- Marimo is gone: code runs in the Workbench, Jupyter or Python in the terminal (To Python and
  `sab.paste()` hand code over).
- "Rerun with the debugger" is not built yet.
